findings.title: Devcontainer dependencies are not immutably pinned
findings.what: The Go image and both devcontainer features are referenced only by mutable tags. Recreating the environment can therefore fetch different publisher-controlled content without a reviewed repository change; the Docker-in-Docker feature has especially broad execution capability.
findings.fix: Pin the image and both feature references to reviewed immutable OCI digests, with an explicit update process for refreshing those digests.
findings.acceptance: Resolve each configured OCI reference twice and verify the file contains an explicit immutable digest for all three dependencies; rebuilding after tag movement must still select the reviewed manifests.
findings.verifyNote: A separate baseline re-read confirmed that lines 3, 5, and 6 contain tag-only references and no digest, checksum, signature policy, or other immutable resolution control.

findings.title: Bootstrap script executes unverified mutable downloads as root
findings.what: The script fetches `latest` kind and kubebuilder executables plus a dynamically selected kubectl executable, marks them executable, and moves them into `/usr/local/bin` without checking a pinned version, checksum, or signature. A compromised redirect, release endpoint, or mutable upstream artifact becomes trusted executable code.
findings.fix: Pin explicit versions, download each artifact and its publisher-provided checksum or signature over HTTPS, verify it before chmod/move, and fail closed on any mismatch.
findings.acceptance: A static check confirms no `latest` or `stable.txt` selector remains and every downloaded executable is verified against a repository-pinned checksum or trusted signature before it is made executable or installed; a deliberately corrupted download makes the script exit nonzero.
findings.verifyNote: The adversarial re-read confirmed all three download-to-execution flows and found no verification command anywhere in the complete 23-line script.

findings.title: Operator image base layers are selected by mutable tags
findings.what: The builder uses `golang:1.25` and the runtime uses `gcr.io/distroless/static:nonroot`, both without immutable digests. Identical source builds can therefore consume different base contents, bypassing review and weakening provenance and rollback reproducibility.
findings.fix: Pin both `FROM` references to reviewed multi-architecture manifest digests while retaining human-readable version tags if desired.
findings.acceptance: Both `FROM` instructions include immutable `@sha256:` digests, and an image build records exactly those reviewed manifests for the intended platforms.
findings.verifyNote: A second full Dockerfile read at the specified baseline confirmed both `FROM` instructions are tag-only and that no later stage or configuration constrains their resolved digests.

findings.title: Dispatch golden image installs an unversioned agent runtime
findings.what: The credential-bearing dispatch image uses mutable `node:24` and runs `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code` without a version or integrity lock. A rebuild can silently install newly published base or CLI code, which then runs alongside runtime OAuth credentials and session data.
findings.fix: Pin the Node base to an OCI digest and install an exact reviewed Claude Code version with verified npm integrity or from a locked artifact; update both pins only through reviewed changes.
findings.acceptance: The `FROM` instruction contains an `@sha256:` digest, the npm install target contains an exact version with integrity verification, and two clean builds from the same source resolve identical base and CLI artifacts.
findings.verifyNote: The separate adversarial pass re-read the complete file and confirmed the base has no digest, the npm package has no version or integrity constraint, and the comment claiming tag-based pinning is not enforced by the Dockerfile.
